# pulse_sso_provider (Resource)

An OpenID Connect provider people can use to sign in to the Pulse dashboard (for example Google Workspace, Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, Authentik or Keycloak).

Register an OAuth client (web application, Authorization Code flow) at the provider with `redirect_uri` as its redirect URI, then set `issuer`, `client_id` and `client_secret` here. Pulse contacts the issuer (OpenID discovery) only when someone signs in, so a wrong issuer shows up at the first sign-in, not at apply. The issuer must use `https`, and Pulse refuses issuers and endpoints on private networks unless `allow_private_network` is set.

New providers are disabled by default. Run a test login from the dashboard (Settings, Single sign-on, Test login) before you enable the provider or turn off password sign-in with `pulse_auth_settings`. Changing `issuer` or `client_id` clears the recorded test login.

Who may sign in: with `provisioning = "preprovisioned"` (the default) only users whose identity is linked with `pulse_user_identity`; with `"jit"` Pulse also creates a user at the first sign-in when every rule in `jit` matches. Map provider groups to roles with `pulse_sso_mapping`.

Deleting the provider unlinks all its identities and removes the roles users got from its group mappings. Import with the provider ID or its slug.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "google_client_secret" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

variable "keycloak_client_secret" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

# Google Workspace sign-in. Register an OAuth client (web application) in the Google Cloud console
# with pulse_sso_provider.google.redirect_uri as its authorized redirect URI.
resource "pulse_sso_provider" "google" {
  slug          = "google"
  display_name  = "Google"
  issuer        = "https://accounts.google.com"
  client_id     = "1234567890-abc.apps.googleusercontent.com"
  client_secret = var.google_client_secret

  # Create users at their first sign-in when they belong to the workspace domain.
  provisioning = "jit"
  jit = {
    email_domains  = ["example.com"]
    hosted_domains = ["example.com"]
  }

  # Enable after a test login from the dashboard (Settings, Single sign-on).
  enabled = true
}

# A Keycloak realm on the home network with a private certificate authority.
resource "pulse_sso_provider" "keycloak" {
  slug                  = "keycloak"
  display_name          = "Home Keycloak"
  issuer                = "https://sso.home.arpa/realms/home"
  client_id             = "pulse"
  client_secret         = var.keycloak_client_secret
  scopes                = ["openid", "profile", "email", "groups"]
  groups_claim          = "groups"
  allow_private_network = true
  ca_bundle_pem         = file("${path.module}/home-ca.pem")
  end_session_enabled   = true
}

output "google_redirect_uri" {
  value = pulse_sso_provider.google.redirect_uri
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `client_id` (String) OAuth client ID registered at the provider (at most 256 bytes).
- `display_name` (String) Name on the sign-in button (at most 64 bytes).
- `issuer` (String) Issuer URL exactly as the provider publishes it in its discovery document (`<issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration`), for example `https://accounts.google.com`. Must use `https` (the dev profile also accepts `http://localhost`).
- `slug` (String) Short name used in sign-in URLs (`/auth/oidc/<slug>/start`): a lowercase letter followed by up to 31 lowercase letters, digits or `-`. Can be changed in place.

### Optional

- `acr_values` (List of String) Authentication context class references to request (`acr_values`), for example to ask the provider for multi-factor sign-in. Default none.
- `allow_cross_origin_endpoints` (Boolean) Allow the discovery document to point to endpoints on another origin than the issuer. Default `false`.
- `allow_private_network` (Boolean) Allow an issuer and endpoints on private or loopback addresses (for a provider in your own network). Default `false`.
- `ca_bundle_pem` (String) PEM certificates to trust for the provider's TLS certificate in addition to the system roots (for a private certificate authority). Default empty.
- `client_secret` (String, Sensitive) OAuth client secret (at most 1024 bytes). Pulse stores it encrypted and never returns it, so it is sent only when created or when its value here changes; removing it from the configuration removes it from Pulse. Leave it out for public clients. A secret changed outside Terraform is not detected unless it was removed.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the provider is offered on the sign-in page. Run a test login first. Default `false`.
- `end_session_enabled` (Boolean) Also sign the person out at the provider when they sign out of Pulse (when the provider supports it). Default `false`.
- `groups_claim` (String) Name of the ID token claim that lists the person's groups (for example `groups`), used by `pulse_sso_mapping` and the `jit.groups` rule. Default empty (no groups).
- `jit` (Attributes) Rules a new person must match to be created at their first sign-in when `provisioning = "jit"`. Every rule that is set must match. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--jit))
- `provisioning` (String) `preprovisioned` (default): only users with a linked identity can sign in. `jit`: Pulse also creates a user at their first sign-in when every rule in `jit` matches (at least one rule is required).
- `scopes` (List of String) Scopes requested at sign-in; must include `openid`. Default `["openid", "profile", "email"]`. Add the scope your provider needs for a groups claim, if any.
- `stepup_fallback` (String) What Pulse does when a sensitive action needs fresh authentication and the provider cannot provide it: `none` (default; sign in with the provider again) or `local_totp` (accept the user's Pulse authenticator code).

### Read-Only

- `has_client_secret` (Boolean) Whether Pulse holds a client secret for this provider.
- `id` (String) Provider ID.
- `redirect_uri` (String) Redirect URI to register at the provider for this client.
- `test_login_ok_at` (String) When an administrator last completed a test login with this provider (RFC 3339), or null. Cleared when `issuer` or `client_id` changes.

<a id="nestedatt--jit"></a>
### Nested Schema for `jit`

Optional:

- `email_domains` (Set of String) Email domains (lower case, such as `example.com`); the ID token must carry a verified email in one of them.
- `groups` (Set of String) Values of the groups claim; the person must be in one of them. Needs `groups_claim`.
- `hosted_domains` (Set of String) Google Workspace domains, matched against the `hd` claim.
- `tenants` (Set of String) Microsoft Entra ID tenant IDs, matched against the `tid` claim.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# By provider ID
terraform import pulse_sso_provider.google 01j9z6t0b1d2e3f4g5h6j7k8m9

# By slug (the client secret is not imported; set it in the configuration and apply)
terraform import pulse_sso_provider.google google
```
